lessons.title: Working tree
lessons.summary: The working tree contains the checked-out files you edit.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The working tree contains the checked-out files you edit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It can differ from both the index and the current commit. Git status separates tracked modifications, staged changes and untracked files. Inspect these states before switching branches or running operations that replace local content.

lessons.takeaway: It can differ from both the index and the current commit. Git status separates tracked modifications, staged changes and untracked files. Inspect these states before switching branches or running operations that replace local content.

lessons.title: Staging
lessons.summary: The index, or staging area, records the exact content intended for the next commit.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The index, or staging area, records the exact content intended for the next commit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: git add copies selected content into the index; later working-tree edits are not automatically staged. Review the staged diff before committing. This allows a coherent commit without including every local change.

lessons.takeaway: git add copies selected content into the index; later working-tree edits are not automatically staged. Review the staged diff before committing. This allows a coherent commit without including every local change.

lessons.title: Commits
lessons.summary: A commit records a tree snapshot, parent relationships and metadata.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A commit records a tree snapshot, parent relationships and metadata.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Commits form a directed history rather than storing only textual patches. A commit's identity changes if its content or metadata changes. Keep commits focused enough that review, rollback and bisection remain useful.

lessons.takeaway: Commits form a directed history rather than storing only textual patches. A commit's identity changes if its content or metadata changes. Keep commits focused enough that review, rollback and bisection remain useful.

lessons.title: Branches
lessons.summary: A branch is a movable reference to a commit.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A branch is a movable reference to a commit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: New commits advance the current branch while other branch references remain where they were. Branches do not provide separate remote permissions by themselves. Worktrees can provide separate checked-out directories for concurrent local work.

lessons.takeaway: New commits advance the current branch while other branch references remain where they were. Branches do not provide separate remote permissions by themselves. Worktrees can provide separate checked-out directories for concurrent local work.

lessons.title: Fetch
lessons.summary: Fetch downloads objects and updates remote-tracking references without merging them into the current branch.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Fetch downloads objects and updates remote-tracking references without merging them into the current branch.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It lets you inspect upstream changes before choosing merge, rebase or another integration strategy. Remote-tracking references describe the last fetched state, not guaranteed real-time remote state.

lessons.takeaway: It lets you inspect upstream changes before choosing merge, rebase or another integration strategy. Remote-tracking references describe the last fetched state, not guaranteed real-time remote state.

lessons.title: Merge
lessons.summary: Merge integrates histories and may create a commit with multiple parents.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Merge integrates histories and may create a commit with multiple parents.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Git finds a common ancestor and combines changes, requiring human resolution when changes conflict. A clean textual merge can still be semantically wrong. Run relevant tests and inspect the combined behavior.

lessons.takeaway: Git finds a common ancestor and combines changes, requiring human resolution when changes conflict. A clean textual merge can still be semantically wrong. Run relevant tests and inspect the combined behavior.

lessons.title: Ignore rules
lessons.summary: Ignore rules keep matching untracked files out of routine Git status and add operations.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Ignore rules keep matching untracked files out of routine Git status and add operations.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They do not remove files already tracked or erase secrets from history. Use them for generated output and local configuration, while handling credential exposure through revocation and an appropriate cleanup process.

lessons.takeaway: They do not remove files already tracked or erase secrets from history. Use them for generated output and local configuration, while handling credential exposure through revocation and an appropriate cleanup process.

lessons.title: Diffs
lessons.summary: A diff compares selected snapshots or file states.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A diff compares selected snapshots or file states.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Plain git diff compares working tree with index; --staged compares index with HEAD. Commit ranges and merge-base comparisons answer different review questions. Choose the comparison explicitly to avoid overlooking staged or upstream changes.

lessons.takeaway: Plain git diff compares working tree with index; --staged compares index with HEAD. Commit ranges and merge-base comparisons answer different review questions. Choose the comparison explicitly to avoid overlooking staged or upstream changes.

lessons.title: Rebase
lessons.summary: Rebase recreates commits on a different base to change history shape.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Rebase recreates commits on a different base to change history shape.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: New commit identities result, and conflicts may need resolution per replayed commit. Avoid rewriting shared history without coordination. Test the final tree because conflict resolutions can alter behavior even when the history looks cleaner.

lessons.takeaway: New commit identities result, and conflicts may need resolution per replayed commit. Avoid rewriting shared history without coordination. Test the final tree because conflict resolutions can alter behavior even when the history looks cleaner.

lessons.title: Revert
lessons.summary: Revert creates a new commit that applies the inverse of an earlier change.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Revert creates a new commit that applies the inverse of an earlier change.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It preserves published history and is often suitable for shared branches. Later changes and merge commits complicate reversal, so review the resulting diff and run tests. Reverting application code does not reverse external database or infrastructure effects.

lessons.takeaway: It preserves published history and is often suitable for shared branches. Later changes and merge commits complicate reversal, so review the resulting diff and run tests. Reverting application code does not reverse external database or infrastructure effects.

lessons.title: Reset
lessons.summary: Reset moves a reference and, depending on mode, changes the index and working tree.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Reset moves a reference and, depending on mode, changes the index and working tree.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Soft reset preserves index and files; mixed reset updates the index; hard reset also replaces tracked working-tree content. Understand which states contain valuable work before choosing a mode. Reflog recovery does not guarantee recovery of uncommitted file content.

lessons.takeaway: Soft reset preserves index and files; mixed reset updates the index; hard reset also replaces tracked working-tree content. Understand which states contain valuable work before choosing a mode. Reflog recovery does not guarantee recovery of uncommitted file content.

lessons.title: Cherry-pick
lessons.summary: Cherry-pick applies the change introduced by a selected commit onto the current branch.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Cherry-pick applies the change introduced by a selected commit onto the current branch.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It creates a new commit identity and may conflict if context differs. Confirm prerequisite changes exist, especially for backports. Copying a single fix without its dependency can compile incorrectly or change behavior unexpectedly.

lessons.takeaway: It creates a new commit identity and may conflict if context differs. Confirm prerequisite changes exist, especially for backports. Copying a single fix without its dependency can compile incorrectly or change behavior unexpectedly.

lessons.title: Conflict resolution
lessons.summary: A conflict requires a deliberate choice about how competing changes should combine.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A conflict requires a deliberate choice about how competing changes should combine.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Read both sides and surrounding intent, resolve the file, stage it and continue the interrupted operation. Removing markers is only a syntactic step. Verify the resulting behavior and ensure no required change was lost.

lessons.takeaway: Read both sides and surrounding intent, resolve the file, stage it and continue the interrupted operation. Removing markers is only a syntactic step. Verify the resulting behavior and ensure no required change was lost.

lessons.title: Reflog
lessons.summary: The reflog records recent movements of local references.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The reflog records recent movements of local references.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It can help locate commits after reset, rebase or accidental branch movement. Entries are local and expire under retention and garbage-collection rules. Find the intended commit and preserve it with a new reference before further cleanup.

lessons.takeaway: It can help locate commits after reset, rebase or accidental branch movement. Entries are local and expire under retention and garbage-collection rules. Find the intended commit and preserve it with a new reference before further cleanup.

lessons.title: Bisect
lessons.summary: Bisection narrows a regression by testing commits between known-good and known-bad points.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Bisection narrows a regression by testing commits between known-good and known-bad points.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A deterministic test lets Git choose intermediate commits efficiently. Skip revisions that cannot be tested for unrelated reasons and restore the original checkout afterward. Flaky tests can point bisection at the wrong change.

lessons.takeaway: A deterministic test lets Git choose intermediate commits efficiently. Skip revisions that cannot be tested for unrelated reasons and restore the original checkout afterward. Flaky tests can point bisection at the wrong change.

lessons.title: Force with lease
lessons.summary: A force push with a lease updates rewritten history only if the remote reference matches an expected value.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A force push with a lease updates rewritten history only if the remote reference matches an expected value.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: An explicit expected commit protects against overwriting an unexpected collaborator update. It remains a history rewrite and requires coordination. Inspect the remote head after a rejected lease instead of retrying blindly.

lessons.takeaway: An explicit expected commit protects against overwriting an unexpected collaborator update. It remains a history rewrite and requires coordination. Inspect the remote head after a rejected lease instead of retrying blindly.

lessons.title: Continuous integration
lessons.summary: CI runs automated checks when changes are proposed or integrated.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CI runs automated checks when changes are proposed or integrated.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Fast, reliable checks catch integration problems near the change. Required checks should validate the actual revision intended for merge. A passing pipeline is limited by its coverage and environment; it is not proof of every production behavior.

lessons.takeaway: Fast, reliable checks catch integration problems near the change. Required checks should validate the actual revision intended for merge. A passing pipeline is limited by its coverage and environment; it is not proof of every production behavior.

lessons.title: Artifacts
lessons.summary: A build artifact is a versioned output produced by a build and consumed by testing or deployment.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A build artifact is a versioned output produced by a build and consumed by testing or deployment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Build once and promote the same immutable artifact where possible. Record its source revision and digest so deployments are traceable. Retention and access policy matter because artifacts can contain proprietary code or sensitive data.

lessons.takeaway: Build once and promote the same immutable artifact where possible. Record its source revision and digest so deployments are traceable. Retention and access policy matter because artifacts can contain proprietary code or sensitive data.

lessons.title: CI secrets
lessons.summary: CI secrets provide credentials to authorized jobs without storing them in source.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CI secrets provide credentials to authorized jobs without storing them in source.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Workflow trust boundaries determine which code can read them. Untrusted pull-request code, logs and uploaded artifacts can leak secrets if privileges are mixed. Prefer short-lived scoped credentials and avoid granting deployment access to arbitrary test code.

lessons.takeaway: Workflow trust boundaries determine which code can read them. Untrusted pull-request code, logs and uploaded artifacts can leak secrets if privileges are mixed. Prefer short-lived scoped credentials and avoid granting deployment access to arbitrary test code.

lessons.title: Dependency pinning
lessons.summary: Dependency pinning constrains the versions or identities used by a build.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Dependency pinning constrains the versions or identities used by a build.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Lock files and immutable action or image references improve reproducibility. A pinned vulnerable dependency still needs updates. Review dependency changes and maintain an intentional refresh process rather than choosing between unrestricted updates and permanent freezing.

lessons.takeaway: Lock files and immutable action or image references improve reproducibility. A pinned vulnerable dependency still needs updates. Review dependency changes and maintain an intentional refresh process rather than choosing between unrestricted updates and permanent freezing.

lessons.title: Caching
lessons.summary: CI caches reuse intermediate data to reduce build time.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CI caches reuse intermediate data to reduce build time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Keys should include inputs that determine validity, such as lock files and platform. Cache contents are an optimization, not a trusted release artifact. Prevent untrusted jobs from poisoning caches consumed by privileged release jobs.

lessons.takeaway: Keys should include inputs that determine validity, such as lock files and platform. Cache contents are an optimization, not a trusted release artifact. Prevent untrusted jobs from poisoning caches consumed by privileged release jobs.

lessons.title: Deployment gates
lessons.summary: Deployment gates require defined checks or decisions before promotion.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Deployment gates require defined checks or decisions before promotion.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Examples include tests, artifact verification, environment approval and health checks. Bind the gate to the actual artifact and destination. An approval for one revision should not silently authorize a different artifact built afterward.

lessons.takeaway: Examples include tests, artifact verification, environment approval and health checks. Bind the gate to the actual artifact and destination. An approval for one revision should not silently authorize a different artifact built afterward.

lessons.title: Rollback
lessons.summary: Rollback returns a deployment to a known compatible version or configuration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Rollback returns a deployment to a known compatible version or configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It requires an available artifact and compatibility with current data and dependencies. Schema or irreversible side effects may require forward recovery instead. Test rollback procedures and measure health after restoration rather than stopping at a successful deployment command.

lessons.takeaway: It requires an available artifact and compatibility with current data and dependencies. Schema or irreversible side effects may require forward recovery instead. Test rollback procedures and measure health after restoration rather than stopping at a successful deployment command.

lessons.title: Concurrency controls
lessons.summary: Concurrency controls prevent conflicting jobs from changing shared deployment state simultaneously.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Concurrency controls prevent conflicting jobs from changing shared deployment state simultaneously.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A deployment lock or queue can serialize updates to one environment while allowing independent work elsewhere. Cancelling a running job may leave partial changes, so define cleanup and recovery. A branch name alone is not a sufficient environment lock.

lessons.takeaway: A deployment lock or queue can serialize updates to one environment while allowing independent work elsewhere. Cancelling a running job may leave partial changes, so define cleanup and recovery. A branch name alone is not a sufficient environment lock.

lessons.title: OIDC federation
lessons.summary: OIDC federation lets a CI workload exchange a signed identity token for short-lived service credentials.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: OIDC federation lets a CI workload exchange a signed identity token for short-lived service credentials.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The receiving trust policy should constrain repository, workflow context and environment as appropriate. Audience and subject validation prevent unintended callers. Short-lived credentials reduce persistence risk but do not make an overprivileged job safe.

lessons.takeaway: The receiving trust policy should constrain repository, workflow context and environment as appropriate. Audience and subject validation prevent unintended callers. Short-lived credentials reduce persistence risk but do not make an overprivileged job safe.

lessons.title: Monorepo checks
lessons.summary: Monorepo checks select validation for several projects stored in one repository.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Monorepo checks select validation for several projects stored in one repository.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Dependency-aware selection is more reliable than checking only directly changed files. Shared libraries, build configuration and tooling can affect many packages. Preserve a full validation path for changes whose impact is uncertain.

lessons.takeaway: Dependency-aware selection is more reliable than checking only directly changed files. Shared libraries, build configuration and tooling can affect many packages. Preserve a full validation path for changes whose impact is uncertain.

lessons.title: Release tags
lessons.summary: A release tag names a chosen commit as a versioned release point.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A release tag names a chosen commit as a versioned release point.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Annotated or signed tags can add metadata and verification, but policies must define trust and immutability. Match the tag, source commit and released artifact digest. Moving a published tag undermines reproducibility for consumers.

lessons.takeaway: Annotated or signed tags can add metadata and verification, but policies must define trust and immutability. Match the tag, source commit and released artifact digest. Moving a published tag undermines reproducibility for consumers.

lessons.title: Flaky tests
lessons.summary: A flaky test produces inconsistent outcomes without a relevant product change.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A flaky test produces inconsistent outcomes without a relevant product change.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Timing, shared state and environmental assumptions are common causes. Track and fix the cause; unlimited retries can hide real regressions. Quarantine needs ownership and a deadline so missing coverage does not become permanent.

lessons.takeaway: Timing, shared state and environmental assumptions are common causes. Track and fix the cause; unlimited retries can hide real regressions. Quarantine needs ownership and a deadline so missing coverage does not become permanent.

lessons.title: Branch protection
lessons.summary: Branch protection and rulesets constrain changes to important branches.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Branch protection and rulesets constrain changes to important branches.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Required reviews, status checks and restricted updates support a controlled integration process. Configure bypass rights deliberately and ensure check names refer to trusted workflows. Repository rules complement, rather than replace, application testing.

lessons.takeaway: Required reviews, status checks and restricted updates support a controlled integration process. Configure bypass rights deliberately and ensure check names refer to trusted workflows. Repository rules complement, rather than replace, application testing.

lessons.title: Supply-chain evidence
lessons.summary: Supply-chain evidence links source, build process and released artifacts.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Supply-chain evidence links source, build process and released artifacts.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Provenance, signatures and dependency inventories support verification and investigation. Verify identity and digest at the deployment boundary. Evidence is only useful when the builder and signing permissions are themselves controlled.

lessons.takeaway: Provenance, signatures and dependency inventories support verification and investigation. Verify identity and digest at the deployment boundary. Evidence is only useful when the builder and signing permissions are themselves controlled.

commands.title: Working state
commands.definition: Summarizes branch and file changes.
commands.purpose: Check for local work before switching or rewriting history.
commands.environment: Read-only; does not show ignored files by default.
commands.interpretation: The two status columns describe index and working-tree changes; ?? means untracked.
commands.safety: Read-only; does not show ignored files by default.

commands.title: Unstaged diff
commands.definition: Compares working-tree content with the index.
commands.purpose: Review edits not yet staged.
commands.environment: Read-only; output may contain secrets introduced locally.
commands.interpretation: Minus lines are removed and plus lines added relative to the index; staged-only changes are absent.
commands.safety: Read-only; output may contain secrets introduced locally.

commands.title: Staged diff
commands.definition: Compares the index with HEAD.
commands.purpose: Review exactly what a normal commit would include.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect before committing.
commands.interpretation: Only staged changes appear; later unstaged edits may differ.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect before committing.

commands.title: Whitespace validation
commands.definition: Checks the selected diff for whitespace errors and conflict-marker problems.
commands.purpose: Catch accidental formatting damage before review.
commands.environment: Read-only; this is not a syntax or semantic test.
commands.interpretation: Output names files and lines with issues; no output usually means no detected issue.
commands.safety: Read-only; this is not a syntax or semantic test.

commands.title: Fetch remote state
commands.definition: Downloads objects and updates origin remote-tracking references.
commands.purpose: Inspect upstream changes without integrating them into the current branch.
commands.environment: Changes local remote-tracking refs and contacts the remote; does not merge.
commands.interpretation: Updated reference ranges show what changed; the working tree stays unchanged.
commands.safety: Changes local remote-tracking refs and contacts the remote; does not merge.

commands.title: History graph
commands.definition: Shows a compact recent commit graph with reference names.
commands.purpose: Understand branching, merges and the current base.
commands.environment: Read-only; the graph is limited to the selected history and count.
commands.interpretation: Stars are commits; connecting lines show parent relationships; labels identify refs.
commands.safety: Read-only; the graph is limited to the selected history and count.

commands.title: Commit details
commands.definition: Displays the current commit summary and file-change statistics.
commands.purpose: Review the scope of the latest commit.
commands.environment: Read-only; statistics do not establish correctness.
commands.interpretation: The stat counts changed lines by file; use a full diff for actual content.
commands.safety: Read-only; statistics do not establish correctness.

commands.title: Branch tracking
commands.definition: Lists local branches with tips and upstream information.
commands.purpose: Find a branch tracking the wrong remote or lacking an upstream.
commands.environment: Read-only; fetch first when current remote state matters.
commands.interpretation: Brackets show upstream and ahead/behind relative to last fetched state.
commands.safety: Read-only; fetch first when current remote state matters.

commands.title: Ignore diagnosis
commands.definition: Explains which ignore pattern matches a path.
commands.purpose: Find why a generated or source file does not appear as expected.
commands.environment: Read-only; replace PATH and remember tracked files are not untracked ignore candidates.
commands.interpretation: Output identifies rule file, line number and pattern.
commands.safety: Read-only; replace PATH and remember tracked files are not untracked ignore candidates.

commands.title: Local recovery history
commands.definition: Shows recent local reference movements.
commands.purpose: Locate a commit lost after reset or rebase.
commands.environment: Read-only; entries expire and do not guarantee recovery of uncommitted changes.
commands.interpretation: Each entry includes a reachable historical tip and the operation that moved it.
commands.safety: Read-only; entries expire and do not guarantee recovery of uncommitted changes.

commands.title: Changed filenames
commands.definition: Lists changes introduced since the merge base with origin/main.
commands.purpose: Review branch scope relative to its base.
commands.environment: Read-only; ensure origin/main is freshly fetched and is the intended comparison branch.
commands.interpretation: A, M and D indicate added, modified and deleted paths; three dots use the merge base.
commands.safety: Read-only; ensure origin/main is freshly fetched and is the intended comparison branch.

commands.title: Release tags
commands.definition: Lists version-like tags in version-aware descending order.
commands.purpose: Inspect available release references.
commands.environment: Read-only; verify tag identity and release artifact separately.
commands.interpretation: Names are tags, not proof that an artifact exists or was verified.
commands.safety: Read-only; verify tag identity and release artifact separately.

commands.title: Repository location
commands.definition: Prints the root of the current working tree.
commands.purpose: Confirm which repository a script or terminal is operating in.
commands.environment: Read-only; verify this before running commands that change index or history.
commands.interpretation: The output is an absolute path; an error means the current location is not inside a recognized working tree.
commands.safety: Read-only; verify this before running commands that change index or history.

commands.title: Configured remotes
commands.definition: Lists remote names and fetch/push URLs.
commands.purpose: Verify where changes will be retrieved from or published to.
commands.environment: Read-only; URLs can contain sensitive credentials in poorly configured repositories.
commands.interpretation: Fetch and push URLs may differ; a familiar remote name does not prove its destination.
commands.safety: Read-only; URLs can contain sensitive credentials in poorly configured repositories.

commands.title: Create a working branch
commands.definition: Creates a branch at the current commit and switches to it.
commands.purpose: Isolate a new change before committing.
commands.environment: Mutates local branch/worktree selection; inspect status and intended starting commit first.
commands.interpretation: The switch confirmation names the new branch; existing uncommitted edits may come along if compatible.
commands.safety: Mutates local branch/worktree selection; inspect status and intended starting commit first.

references.title: Create a working branch — primary documentation

commands.title: Stage selected hunks
commands.definition: Interactively stages chosen changes from a file.
commands.purpose: Separate unrelated edits into reviewable commits.
commands.environment: Mutates the index, not the remote; only stage understood changes.
commands.interpretation: Each hunk prompt asks whether to stage the shown diff; review git diff --staged afterward.
commands.safety: Mutates the index, not the remote; only stage understood changes.

commands.title: Unstage without discarding
commands.definition: Restores an index entry from HEAD while retaining working-tree edits.
commands.purpose: Remove an accidental file change from the next commit.
commands.environment: Mutates the index. Do not omit --staged if the intention is to keep working-tree changes.
commands.interpretation: Usually silent on success; git status and git diff show the retained unstaged work.
commands.safety: Mutates the index. Do not omit --staged if the intention is to keep working-tree changes.

commands.title: Create a local commit
commands.definition: Creates a commit from the staged snapshot.
commands.purpose: Record one reviewed change with a useful explanation.
commands.environment: Mutates local history and can run repository hooks. Review staged content and test results first.
commands.interpretation: The summary gives a new commit ID and file statistics; unstaged edits remain outside it.
commands.safety: Mutates local history and can run repository hooks. Review staged content and test results first.

references.title: Create a local commit — primary documentation

commands.title: Inspect a complete commit
commands.definition: Displays commit metadata and its patch.
commands.purpose: Understand exactly what a candidate release or recovery commit changed.
commands.environment: Read-only; replace COMMIT with a verified reference.
commands.interpretation: Author and Commit dates can differ; the patch shows the change relative to parent context.
commands.safety: Read-only; replace COMMIT with a verified reference.

references.title: Inspect a complete commit — primary documentation

commands.title: Find line history
commands.definition: Shows the last recorded change attribution for selected lines.
commands.purpose: Find relevant history before modifying unfamiliar behavior.
commands.environment: Read-only; follow the referenced commits to understand surrounding changes.
commands.interpretation: Each line includes a commit ID, author metadata and line content; attribution is not proof of fault or original design intent.
commands.safety: Read-only; follow the referenced commits to understand surrounding changes.

commands.title: Fast-forward integration
commands.definition: Updates the current branch only if the integration can fast-forward.
commands.purpose: Avoid silently creating a merge commit when synchronizing a linear branch.
commands.environment: Mutates the local branch and files; preserve uncommitted work and confirm the current branch first.
commands.interpretation: Fast-forward output means no merge commit was needed; failure means histories diverged and need an explicit decision.
commands.safety: Mutates the local branch and files; preserve uncommitted work and confirm the current branch first.

commands.title: Reverse a published change
commands.definition: Creates a new change that reverses a selected commit.
commands.purpose: Undo an approved bad change while preserving published history.
commands.environment: Mutates files/history; review dependent changes and special handling for merge commits before use.
commands.interpretation: A new commit is created after any conflicts are resolved; external effects and database migrations are not automatically reversed.
commands.safety: Mutates files/history; review dependent changes and special handling for merge commits before use.

references.title: Reverse a published change — primary documentation

commands.title: Apply a selected fix
commands.definition: Applies a commit's patch as a new commit on the current branch.
commands.purpose: Backport an isolated verified fix.
commands.environment: Mutates branch and working tree; inspect prerequisites and run relevant tests.
commands.interpretation: The new commit usually has a different ID; conflict messages require semantic resolution, not blind marker removal.
commands.safety: Mutates branch and working tree; inspect prerequisites and run relevant tests.

references.title: Apply a selected fix — primary documentation

commands.title: Preserve temporary work
commands.definition: Stores tracked edits and untracked files, then cleans them from the working tree.
commands.purpose: Temporarily set aside work before a local investigation.
commands.environment: Mutates local files; inspect the stash and avoid treating it as a remote backup.
commands.expectedOutput: Saved working directory and index state ...
commands.interpretation: The saved message identifies a local stash; ignored files are not included by -u.
commands.safety: Mutates local files; inspect the stash and avoid treating it as a remote backup.

commands.title: Inspect a stash
commands.definition: Displays the patch represented by a stash entry.
commands.purpose: Check saved work before restoring it.
commands.environment: Read-only; sensitive edits remain visible in the patch.
commands.interpretation: The diff shows changes in that stash; confirm the entry name because new stashes change numeric positions.
commands.safety: Read-only; sensitive edits remain visible in the patch.

commands.title: Start regression bisection
commands.definition: Starts binary-search selection between known bad and good revisions.
commands.purpose: Narrow a reproducible regression to its introducing commit.
commands.environment: Changes the checkout, usually to detached HEAD. Preserve edits first and use git bisect reset to finish.
commands.interpretation: Git checks out a candidate and reports remaining steps; mark each candidate good or bad after the same reliable test.
commands.safety: Changes the checkout, usually to detached HEAD. Preserve edits first and use git bisect reset to finish.

commands.title: Exit regression bisection
commands.definition: Ends a bisect session and returns to the original checkout.
commands.purpose: Restore normal development context after finding or abandoning a regression search.
commands.environment: Mutates checkout state; inspect local changes before ending a session.
commands.expectedOutput: Previous HEAD position was ... Switched to branch ...
commands.interpretation: The checkout summary identifies the restored branch/commit; any test-created edits still need inspection.
commands.safety: Mutates checkout state; inspect local changes before ending a session.

commands.title: Separate working tree
commands.definition: Creates another working tree with a new branch.
commands.purpose: Review or implement independent work without disturbing the current checkout.
commands.environment: Writes a directory and creates a branch. Choose an unused destination and verify the base ref.
commands.interpretation: The destination contains its own working files while sharing repository objects.
commands.safety: Writes a directory and creates a branch. Choose an unused destination and verify the base ref.

commands.title: Annotated release tag
commands.definition: Creates a local annotated tag for a verified commit.
commands.purpose: Record release metadata before an authorized publication.
commands.environment: Mutates local refs; confirm version, target commit and release policy before creating or pushing.
commands.interpretation: Usually silent; inspect with git show v1.2.3. This does not publish the tag or prove artifact provenance.
commands.safety: Mutates local refs; confirm version, target commit and release policy before creating or pushing.

commands.title: Compare release contents
commands.definition: Summarizes file changes between two revisions.
commands.purpose: Check the scope of a candidate release before reading detailed patches.
commands.environment: Read-only; verify both reference identities and inspect substantive patches separately.
commands.interpretation: Each row shows a file and insertion/deletion counts; statistics alone cannot prove correctness.
commands.safety: Read-only; verify both reference identities and inspect substantive patches separately.

debugging.title: Accidental local reset
debugging.symptom: A developer moved the branch tip and cannot find a committed change.

steps.evidence: Locate the prior tip and inspect the commit before changing refs. Distinguish committed work from uncommitted content, which reflog may not recover.
Create a recovery branch at the verified commit, then integrate deliberately. Avoid more destructive cleanup until useful work is preserved.
Compare recovered files and run relevant tests; confirm no collaborator history was overwritten.

debugging.title: Published bad commit
debugging.symptom: A merged commit introduces a production regression.

steps.evidence: Identify the change and later dependencies; compare code rollback with current schema and external effects.
Create a reviewed revert when compatible, or a forward fix when reversal would damage data. Preserve shared history rather than force-resetting main.
Run regression tests and verify production behavior after deploying the chosen recovery artifact.

debugging.title: Merge conflict hides logic loss
debugging.symptom: Conflict markers are removed but one branch's behavior is missing.

steps.evidence: Review the common intent of both changes and inspect surrounding code, not only the marked lines.
Resolve the semantic combination explicitly and add or run a test covering both requirements. Abort and restart the integration if the resolution is unclear.
Verify both original behaviors and the combined path before committing the merge result.

references.title: Merge conflict hides logic loss — primary documentation

debugging.title: CI passes but deployment differs
debugging.symptom: The deployed application does not match the revision that passed tests.

steps.evidence: Trace source commit, build artifact digest and deployment record. Check whether a later rebuild or mutable tag substituted different bytes.
Promote the tested immutable artifact and bind deployment gates to its digest. Correct the pipeline's source-to-artifact evidence.
Verify the running artifact digest and expected behavior, then test that a changed artifact cannot bypass the gate.

references.title: CI passes but deployment differs — primary documentation

debugging.title: Secret committed to repository
debugging.symptom: A credential appears in a commit and CI logs.

steps.evidence: Identify the credential's exposure, readers, artifacts and active uses without printing it again. Removing the latest file does not invalidate prior copies.
Revoke or rotate the credential first, repair consumers and follow the repository's history/artifact cleanup procedure. Add appropriate secret prevention checks.
Confirm the old credential is unusable, consumers use the replacement and future test commits are detected before publication.

references.title: Secret committed to repository — primary documentation

debugging.title: Flaky test blocks releases
debugging.symptom: The same revision alternates between pass and failure.

steps.evidence: Compare failure signatures, timing, shared resources and test order. Determine whether the flake masks an actual product race.
Fix isolation or synchronization; if temporary quarantine is necessary, assign an owner and expiry while preserving critical coverage elsewhere.
Run the meaningful reproduction repeatedly under varied order/load and confirm stable results without unlimited retries.

references.title: Flaky test blocks releases — primary documentation

debugging.title: Concurrent deployments collide
debugging.symptom: Two CI jobs update the same environment and leave mixed versions.

steps.evidence: Compare deployment timestamps, artifact identities and shared-state changes. Check whether cancellation left a partially applied operation.
Serialize per-environment deployments and reconcile to one known-good artifact. Define safe cancellation and recovery for partial updates.
Run overlapping test deployments and verify only one writer operates while final environment state matches a single recorded release.

debugging.title: Dependency update breaks builds
debugging.symptom: A build fails without application-source changes.

steps.evidence: Inspect lock-file changes, toolchain versions, mutable references and cache keys. A stale cache can also obscure the actual dependency set.
Pin reproducible inputs, invalidate the affected cache appropriately and test the dependency update separately. Do not broadly downgrade unrelated packages.
Build from a clean environment and verify the same inputs produce the intended tested artifact.

references.title: Dependency update breaks builds — primary documentation

debugging.title: OIDC credential exchange denied
debugging.symptom: A deployment job cannot obtain its cloud role credentials.

steps.evidence: Inspect the job identity-token permission, audience and trust-policy subject conditions. Repository, branch or environment identity may differ from the allowed context.
Correct the narrow workflow permission or trust condition for the intended release path. Do not allow every repository or pull request to assume the deployment role.
Test the authorized job and confirm an untrusted branch or repository remains denied.

references.title: OIDC credential exchange denied — primary documentation

debugging.title: Regression origin unclear
debugging.symptom: A bug exists on main but the introducing commit is unknown.

steps.evidence: Choose verified good and bad revisions and a deterministic reproduction. Confirm unrelated build failures can be distinguished from the bug.
Use controlled bisection with the reproduction, inspect the identified change and create a focused fix. Preserve local work before changing checkouts.
Run the reproduction against the parent, culprit and fix and verify neighboring behavior remains correct.
